== Biography ==
'''Jean Glasgow''' was baptised at Dundonald, Ayrshire, on 01 Oct 1732. The parish register names her father as [[Glasgow-3586|William Glasgow]].<ref name="FMP1" /> Because the entry records a baptism rather than a birth, her birth is placed before that date, and Dundonald is inferred from the baptism rather than independently recorded.

== Research Notes ==
=== Dundonald family assessment ===

[[Stevenson-14560|Barbara Stevenson]] is the confidently identified mother of [[Glasgow-4101|William Glasgow]], assessed at 99% subjective confidence. His retained Findmypast transcript records a Dundonald baptism on 12 June 1733 and explicitly names Barbara Stevenson as mother (OPR 590/1, item 3, p.82; SCOT/OPR/BAP/3536725). FamilySearch XYZB-Z9Z concerns this same 1733 child. The two indexes represent one underlying register, not independent historical corroboration.

Select [[Glasgow-3586|William Glasgow]], the weaver at Achenyeards named as Jean’s father in the 1 October 1732 Dundonald baptism, as [[Glasgow-4101|William Glasgow]]’s possible father at 52% subjective confidence. The children share the uncommon surname and parish, their entries occur on nearby pages of the same register, and the boy’s William name agrees with the proposed father. The proposed father’s association with Barbara Stevenson is tree-derived; no inspected marriage or entry naming both parents corroborates that pairing. The whole father proposition remains an indirect household reconstruction.

The 1733 transcript has no father field or residence; absence from a transcript does not establish what the manuscript contains or prove illegitimacy. The 1732 transcript names William, weaver at Achenyeards, but no mother. Their baptisms are only 254 days apart, about eight and a half months: close spacing weakens a routine successive-infant-birth interpretation, while unknown birth dates and possible delayed baptism leave the proposed siblings compatible. Do not manufacture birth dates to resolve it. Another Glasgow father, a different Barbara Stevenson, and two separate local families remain alternatives. Barbara’s identification with her own 1733 citation is strong; the adult couple and cross-child father assignment are separate inferences. Jean’s transcript names no mother, and shared maternity of the two children remains unproved. The earlier Ayrshire William accounts [[Glasgow-1055]], [[Glasgow-3288]] and [[Glasgow-1061]] remain compatible wider comparisons; estimated ages or missing family details do not exclude them. No record links this father to any of their birth families, so no upstream father is selected. Identification of this child with later newspaper, maritime or American Williams remains unproved.  Original register images have not been inspected for this assessment.<ref>[https://www.findmypast.co.uk/transcript?id=SCOT%2FOPR%2FBAP%2F3536725&tab=this Findmypast retained transcript: William, 12 June 1733, Dundonald OPR590/1 item3 p.82; mother Barbara Stevenson; father field absent]; [https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:XYZB-Z9Z FamilySearch XYZB-Z9Z: the same 1733 baptism cited by Barbara’s existing profile; citation reused, record page not newly inspected]; [https://www.findmypast.co.uk/transcript?id=SCOT%2FOPR%2FBAP%2F3536699&tab=this Findmypast retained transcript: Jean, 1 October 1732, Dundonald OPR590/1 item3 p.80; father William, weaver, Achenyeards; mother absent]. Maintained transcripts and citation, not newly inspected original pages.</ref>

The baptism is the only record found for Jean Glasgow. A search of live WikiTree profiles found no compatible match; [[Glasgow-1344|Jean]], [[Glasgow-1506|Jean]], [[Glasgow-3489|Jean]], [[Glasgow-810|Jean]] belongs to a different family and is not this person.

A possible identification concerns Jean Glasgow. The banns/marriage index records Jeane Glasgow and Robert Aliesone on 28 May 1652 at St Monance.<ref>Scotland’s People: Old Parish Registers — banns and marriages: OPR 454/10 / 169; [https://www.scotlandspeople.gov.uk/ record].</ref> The original parish register image has not been inspected. The combined index date does not by itself identify the precise event type. The identification remains uncertain.

A possible identification concerns Jean Glasgow. The printed Edinburgh marriage register records Jean Glasgow with William Mitchell, merchant, on 16 December 1675.<ref>Scotland’s People: Old Parish Registers — banns and marriages: OPR 685 / 1/440 / 164; [https://www.scotlandspeople.gov.uk/ record]; Henry Paton, ed., Register of Marriages for the Parish of Edinburgh, 1595–1700 (Scottish Record Society, 1905), printed pp.267 and 481; PDF pp.277 and 491; [https://electricscotland.com/history/records/scottishrecordso16scotuoft.pdf#page=491 record]; Same edition, unnumbered Prefatory Note, PDF p.9; [https://electricscotland.com/history/records/scottishrecordso16scotuoft.pdf#page=9 record].</ref> The printed transcription and its preface were visually inspected on 30 September 2026; original parish image unchecked. The identification remains uncertain.

A possible identification concerns Jean Glasgow. The banns/marriage index records Jean Glasgow and Robert Woodsyd on 13 January 1700 at West Kilbride.<ref>Scotland’s People: Old Parish Registers — banns and marriages: OPR 620/20 / 77; [https://www.scotlandspeople.gov.uk/ record].</ref> The original parish register image has not been inspected. The combined index date does not by itself identify the precise event type. Jean Glasgow/Robert Woodsyd 1700 has no compatible proven pair; [[Woodside-936]] was born 1696. The identification remains uncertain.
